chapter: Taped excerpts: friends, family and facts
title: Handy as 'Father of the Blues'; setting the record straight
summary: Johnson says such titles just happen, and cannot name offhand what he wants corrected.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Wonderful. Wonderful. We were talking about W. C. Handy the other day. And one of the things that I asked you, you know, you had mentioned that he was a school-teacher. How do you suppose he got to be called the "Father of the Blues?" How does something like that --
Those things happen all during life. (inaudible). How did Paul Whiteman become "King of Blues?" King of --
Yes. I know that you're really interested -- I know that you're really interested in setting the record straight --

-- with jazz, which is so important, because you're one of the few people who can do it. Now -- and we have the information where they've called you Jimmy when your name was J. C. We have the information where their background information on you is all wrong. And we -- you know, we've corrected that.
What are other things -- what are other things that you would really like to see straightened out, certain things in setting the record straight?
Well, just offhand that's just a little difficult to say because I would have to give that situation back to (inaudible). And I couldn't say that just offhand.
